about: Round 732. Every row of public.tennis_grand_slam_winners, read with SELECT through the Supabase MCP on 2026-09-30, checked champion by champion against the event's official champions list and ESPN's Grand Slam history tables. scripts/simTennisSlams.mjs holds supabase/migrations/20260930_round_732_tennis_slams.sql to this record.

snapshot.md5Of: md5(string_agg(id || '|' || year || '|' || tournament || '|' || category || '|' || coalesce(champion,'<NULL>'), E'\n' order by id))

method: A row is verified when the official list and the second source name the same player for that year, allowing the married and maiden names of one player (listed under nameVariants). The printed field keeps what each source prints, in source order. Where the two disagreed a third source settled it and the note says which.
usOpenFeed: https://www.usopen.org/en_US/json/man/past_champions.json is one feed for every US Open event despite the "man" in its path: fetched 2026-09-30 it carries 19 sections, among them ms (Men's Singles Champions 1881-2026, 147 rows) and ws (Women's Singles Champions 1887-2026, 140 rows), each row a year, champion, runner-up and score. There is no separate women's feed (json/woman/ and json/women/ both answer 404). The 140 US Open Women's Singles rows and the 2026 Rybakina fill were checked against the ws section of this feed, so the URL on those rows is the page that lists them. The ws section prints 2026 as champion Elena Rybakina, runner-up Aryna Sabalenka, 64 57 62; the ms section prints 2026 as champion Alexander Zverev, runner-up Ben Shelton, 63 76(2) 57 62.
nameVariants: The table stores some players under the name used that year and some under a later name: Margaret Smith and Margaret Court, Helen Wills, Helen Wills Moody and Helen Moody, Margaret Osborne and Margaret Osborne duPont, Molla Bjurstedt and Molla Mallory, Blanche Bingley and Blanche Hillyard, Charlotte Cooper and Charlotte Sterry, Dorothea Douglass and Dorothea Lambert Chambers, Kitty McKane and Kitty Godfree, Hazel Hotchkiss Wightman, Ann Haydon and Ann Haydon Jones and Ann Jones, Evonne Goolagong (Cawley), Chris Evert (Lloyd), Justine Henin (Hardenne). Each is the right player; the split is recorded here and left for a round that decides one display name per player.
score: The score column held no score on any row: 1,010 rows carried a three letter nation code (apparently the runner-up's, from a shifted scrape), 7 carried footnote debris such as "[ h ]" or "Peru", and 2 were NULL. No reader selects it. The migration sets every score without a digit to NULL. Every stored value is kept below under scores, keyed by id, read through the public REST API on 2026-09-30 from the same 1,019 rows the snapshot md5 covers, so the wipe can be reversed from this file alone.
notInScope: runner_up is NULL on every row, so Tennis Chain still cannot check a defeat; the official sources used here carry the runner-up and could fill it in a later round.

confirmed2026.about: The six 2026 champions were past the round's own knowledge, so a fixer with network confirmed each on 2026-09-30 against the official list or feed and a second organisation. Every URL here was opened or returned by search that day.
confirmed2026.wartimeRows: The ten dropped rows (1941 to 1945, French Open, both singles events) were checked the same day: https://www.rolandgarros.com/en-us/palmares lists men's and women's champions for 1939 and 1946 and nothing between, and both ESPN tables (https://www.espn.com/tennis/history and https://www.espn.com/tennis/history/_/type/women) likewise carry no French Open row for 1940 to 1945. The 1901 women's row prints P. Girod on both.

followUps: Re-bake src/data/tennisHLPlayers.ts after the migration lands: Sinner 5, Zverev 2, Andreeva, Nosková and Rybakina gain a title, Goolagong's exclusion reason (the missing December 1977 row) no longer holds.
Fill runner_up from the same sources; the US Open feed carries runner-up and score for every row of both singles events.
Record the round and the unapplied migration in docs/PROJECT-STATE.md and docs/WORKBOARD.md at assembly.
